title: The benefits of doing nothing
reason: 从昨日的金融科技与能源决策主题轮换到生产力和工作生活平衡。节目讨论休息、团队协作、备用能力与注意力恢复，适合联系平台值班、故障响应、项目节奏和工程团队韧性；练习围绕六个高频表达重复调用，从原文支撑逐步过渡到改写、受限工作场景应用和有限自由表达。

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does Beth mean when she says she is 'kicking back'?

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The vocabulary review defines 'kick back' as stopping what you are doing and relaxing completely.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: In a world of constant stimulation, what does it mean to 'switch off'?

assessment.retellingPrompt: Retell the episode in 80-120 words without looking at the full transcript. Use this structure: (1) topic - why doing nothing may have benefits; (2) two key ideas - inactive ants as a reserve and boredom as a source of curiosity; (3) conclusion or example - how people can make space to relax. Phrase bank: 'at any given time', 'ready to step in', 'switch off'. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, clear English is enough; advanced vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: Even animals known for being busy spend significant periods doing nothing.
Research on rock ants suggests that roughly half of a colony is inactive at any given time.
One possible explanation is that inactive ants form a reserve ready to help if disease or disaster strikes.
Psychologist Sandi Mann argues that productivity is overrated and boredom can encourage curiosity and invention.
Constant stimulation, swiping and scrolling make it harder for people to relax and tolerate boredom.
The programme suggests that switching off and slowing down can help people experience the benefits of boredom.
